channel.title: WSJ | World
channel.description: WSJ World News RSS, without Opinions

item.title: Canada Building Permits Rebound in August
item.description: The total value of building permits rose 8.8% from the month before to a seasonally adjusted 13.57 billion Canadian dollars, the equivalent of $9.55 billion, Statistics Canada said.

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts of October 2026: Up to 5.00%
item.description: Beat average interest rates with one of these top high-yield savings accounts.

item.title: Ukraine Says New Limits on Starlink Are Disrupting Its Military Operations
item.description: Ukrainian officials say the limits imposed on the terminals have blunted their ability to attack Russian targets and intercept drones.

item.title: Nord Stream Trial Tests Germany’s Alliance With Ukraine
item.description: A Ukrainian officer is on trial for war crimes related to blowing up the pipelines, testing the limits of wartime sabotage and Germany’s alliance with Kyiv.

item.title: How Kimberly Guilfoyle Lost Trump’s Confidence and Her Job in Greece
item.description: Plus, U.S. airstrikes are failing to stop the global cocaine boom, and a Saudi national is charged with bugging OpenAI’s office.

item.title: Houthi Strike Hits Building at Saudi Aramco Headquarters
item.description: The attack follows strikes on Riyadh’s international airport and expands the conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-backed militants.

item.title: EU Accepts Sanofi’s Concessions to End Antitrust Probe Over Vaccine Marketing
item.description: Sanofi’s offer to rectify the potential effects of its past messages on a rival flu shot awould address concerns, the bloc’s executive arm said.

item.title: BOE’s Pill ‘Skeptical’ Four Rate Rises Needed to Tame Inflation
item.description: The central bank’s chief economist said the size of the response that is now needed to contain inflation may not be as large investors now expect.

item.title: Chinese Exports Soar in September
item.description: Exports rose 36.3% from a year earlier in September, beating market expectations and potentially threatening to heighten trade tensions with major partners.

item.title: The Houthis Are Building an Advanced Missile With Chinese Parts
item.description: A report by weapons experts at Conflict Armament Research shows how the Yemeni militant group is developing medium-range weapons independently of Iran.

item.title: Why U.S. Airstrikes Are Failing to Stop the Global Cocaine Boom
item.description: Smugglers are shifting routes and using new tactics to evade military targeting, resulting in record supplies and plunging prices.

item.title: Pope Leo Diagnosed With Lung Cancer After Surgery
item.description: The 71-year-old pontiff underwent an operation to remove the lower lobe of his right lung.

item.title: Oil Ends Mixed as Traders Weigh Middle East Risks, Russian Diesel Supplies
item.description: Oil prices were mixed as traders weighed persistent Middle East supply risks against prospects for additional Russian diesel exports.

item.title: Drone Attacks on Ships Sailing Near NATO Waters Present Fresh Threat for the Alliance
item.description: European leaders, who have accused Russia of brazen assaults on their soil, contend with strikes on ships skirting their waters.

item.title: U.S. Defense Startups Flock to Taiwan to Build China-Free Drones
item.description: The emerging industry has the potential to serve the U.S. military while providing Taiwan with an arsenal that it sees as essential to its survival.

item.title: While Trump Floats a Kim Meeting, North Korea Flaunts Its U.S.-Range Missiles
item.description: Kim Jong Un took his family to a new military museum, where drones and missiles underscore a push to advance his military.

item.title: Kimberly-Clark, Kenvue Win Conditional EU Approval for $40 Billion Tie-Up
item.description: The European Commission—the EU’s executive arm—said that the sale fully addresses officials’ earlier concerns that the deal could hinder competition in tampon markets in Czechia, Estonia, and Slovakia.

item.title: U.K. Spy Agency Confronts Escalating Hybrid War With Russia and Iran
item.description: The head of MI5 has painted a sobering picture of a range of threats now facing Britain and European allies.

item.title: The Morning Risk Report: Trump’s Diesel Deal With Russia Faces Questions From Lawmakers on Legality
item.description: Plus: U.K. floats payments for fraud whistleblowers and Delta delays Saudi Arabia plans.

item.title: A Demographic Mirage May Be Distorting China’s Economic Ambitions
item.description: Plus, Beijing’s tepid recovery efforts, falling government bond yields and why China resists joining the developed world.
